exposure: Mode of birth (lower segment cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
cohort: The study included 791 neonates from southern India, comprising those admitted for >48h in NICUs in Vellore (2014-2015) and Chennai (2015-2016), and neonates born in Vellore hospitals but not admitted to NICUs (2015-2016).
finding: The study demonstrated the widespread persistence of the G10P[11] rotavirus strain in southern India, with high positivity rates (29.5-54%) among neonates.
mod_finding: Neonates delivered by lower segment cesarean section had a significantly higher odds of acquiring rotavirus infection compared to those delivered vaginally [OR = 2.4 (1.4-4.3)].
cross-section timing: Stool samples were collected from 2014-2016 across different neonatal care settings.
